name: Shared rings and distant light flashes: four field conditions (Dotta 2011)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Dotta, Buckner, Lafrenie & Persinger 2011), shared circumcerebral rings
summary: The magnetic half of Dotta, Buckner, Lafrenie & Persinger 2011: two people 10 m apart wear identical eight-coil rings running four counter-clockwise field conditions (20+2, 20-2, 100+10, 100-10) while one of them watches dim 7-8 Hz light flashes in 30-s trains. Persinger's lab reported a small rise in photon emission beside the right hemisphere of the other, blindfolded partner in the dark, and one of three such partners reported seeing 'white light' in 5 of 6 flash intervals.
notes: Verified from the abstract and Persinger & Lavallee 2010 section 3.7: response partner blindfolded in a dark room 10 m away, a photomultiplier tube 15 cm from the right hemisphere at the level of the temporal lobes; 7-8 Hz flashes of about 1 lux, 30 s on and 30 s off; field conditions of 2-5 min with base and change durations of 20+2, 20-2, 100+10 and 100-10; a net increase of about 10^-11 W/m2; 3 pairs. In the lab's notation "20+2" is 20, 18 ... 6 ms over the 8 coils, "20-2" 20, 22 ... 34 ms, "100+10" 100, 90 ... 30 ms and "100-10" 100, 110 ... 170 ms. The order and length of the conditions in the human study are not given: each runs 5 min here, accelerating before decelerating, as in the lab's standard primer/effector sequence (Dotta & Persinger 2012; the statement that the effect needed that order comes from its chemistry and cell work, not from this human study). The waveforms are inferred from that sequence: the accelerating conditions carry the decreasing-frequency Thomas pattern (the exact 849-point patent table; the lab's file had 859 points) and the decelerating ones the increasing-frequency burst-firing pattern (230 points, values never published, so the built-in accelerating burst stands in, 18 to 90 Hz), both at 1 ms per point as in Dotta & Persinger 2012 and repeated back to back. Ring: Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2 (coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal, within 5 degrees of the 45-degree ring). Both helmets run this program and start together (the lab drove both rings from one controller). Source cautions: photon counts of 10^-11 W/m2 are at instrument noise and any home attempt will measure light leaks; no blinding of the PMT operator is described; flashing light can trigger seizures in susceptible people. 3 pairs, single lab, never independently replicated. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Do not use results for decisions about real people. Nobody with epilepsy, a seizure history or photosensitivity should take part in either role.
setting: Partner A (light): closed, quiet room, helmet on, watching a diffuse white light of about 1 lux flashing at 7-8 Hz in 30-s trains. Partner B: blindfolded in a dark room 10 m away, second helmet running this program; the lab measured photon emission 15 cm from the right side of B's head. A test that needs no photomultiplier (a project addition): B says 'now' whenever light seems to appear and a helper logs the times; A starts the trains at irregular times from a hidden list, compared with B's log only afterwards.
schedule: One session per pair. As a control, repeat on another day with the light covered or both helmets on sham (set by a helper, the same for both) and compare B's hit rates blind.
source: Dotta, Buckner, Lafrenie & Persinger 2011, Brain Res 1388:77-88 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21396353/ ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, Theoretical and experimental evidence of macroscopic entanglement between human brain activity and photon emissions, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (20+2 notation; coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Dotta & Persinger 2012, "Doubling" of local photon emissions when two simultaneous, spatially-separated, chemiluminescent reactions share the same magnetic field configurations, J Biophys Chem 3:72-80 (859- and 230-point patterns at 1 ms; primer/effector order) https://file.scirp.org/Html/17181.html ; Lehman 2016, PhD thesis, Laurentian University ("20-2" = 20, 22 ... 34 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/e7b03302-1b7f-4f4f-acf5-bdf41ee5370f/content ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse point values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Juden-Kelly, Dotta, Vares & Persinger 2015, JCER 6(9):728-737 (Burst-X: 230 points) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/497 ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University (230-point burst-firing file) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
